patients.summary: Retired administrative assistant with type 2 diabetes and hypertension who joins in 2020. Later years bring genitourinary syndrome of menopause, urge incontinence on mirabegron, a torus palatinus, an ACE-inhibitor cough, drug-induced diffuse alveolar hemorrhage after TMP-SMX, and left T8 zoster with later neuropathic pain.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller wants to become a patient here. Her old primary care office is cutting back and she wants a doctor she can actually reach. Retired, commercial BCBS plan. Has diabetes and blood pressure, on four meds. Explained membership and that insurance still covers labs, imaging and specialists. New patient visit booked 9/14 at 9:00, asked her to come fasting and to bring her pill bottles. Records release sent to prior practice by fax.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
54 yo woman establishing care. Prior PCP office downsizing.

Diabetes: told about 6 years ago on routine labs. Metformin 1000 twice a day the whole time, never on insulin or anything else. Doesn't check sugars at home much. Last A1c she remembers was "around 7." No eye or foot problems she knows of. Sees an optometrist yearly.
Hypertension: about 8 years. Lisinopril 20 and HCTZ 12.5, both in the morning. Doesn't own a cuff.
Atorvastatin 20 started by her old doctor "because of the diabetes." No muscle aches.

Other hx: menopause at 52, no hormones ever, no bleeding since. Chickenpox as a kid. Has lost several teeth over the years and had them pulled; partial edentulism, wears nothing currently.
No surgeries otherwise. No known drug allergies.
FH: mother T2DM; father HTN; paternal grandfather heart disease.
SH: retired admin assistant (school district office). Lives alone in Greenfield. Never smoked, no alcohol.
Health maintenance per pt: colonoscopy ~3 yrs ago normal, Pap last year normal, mammogram this past spring. Records requested.

ROS otherwise negative.
Exam: well, pleasant. BP as charted. HEENT: partial edentulism, oropharynx clear. Neck supple, no thyromegaly. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, NT. Ext no edema. Feet: skin intact, monofilament intact bilaterally, DP pulses 2+.
PHQ-2 0.

A/P
1. T2DM, on metformin. A1c, UACR today.
2. HTN, at goal today on lisinopril/HCTZ. CMP.
3. Statin for diabetes, continue. Lipids.
4. HM: HCV and HIV screen once today. Flu shot in Oct. Mammo due spring. Colonoscopy and Pap per records.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Sheila, your labs are back. A1c is about where you guessed, which is reasonable control. Kidney function, liver tests, blood counts and potassium are all normal, and there is no protein leaking in the urine. LDL is in a good place on the atorvastatin. Hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. No changes for now, see you in December.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care practice
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Received by fax, 38 pages, 2016 to 2020. Summary abstracted by MA:
- Problem list: type 2 diabetes (since 2014), hypertension (since 2012), postmenopausal.
- Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily.
- Allergies: NKDA.
- Colonoscopy 2017: normal to cecum, no polyps; repeat in 10 years.
- Pap with HPV co-test 2019: NILM, HPV negative.
- Screening mammogram March 2020: BI-RADS 1.
- Last A1c Feb 2020 7.1%.
- Tdap 2016. Influenza most years.
Scanned to chart, routed to PCP for review.

documents.title: Flu vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Quadrivalent flu 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. No prior reactions, feels well today. VIS reviewed. Tolerated, left after 15 minutes.

documents.title: Diabetic eye exam report
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Dilated diabetic eye examination, date of service 11/10/2020.
VA 20/25 OD, 20/25 OS with correction. IOP normal. Lenses clear. Fundus: no diabetic retinopathy either eye, maculae flat. Recommend annual exam.
Thank you for the referral.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Doing fine. Walking her neighborhood when weather allows, less lately. Taking meds without missed doses. No hypoglycemia, no polyuria. Eye exam done last month, no retinopathy.
O: vitals as charted. Lungs clear, heart regular. Feet without lesions.
A/P: T2DM, HTN stable on current regimen. A1c and BMP today. Prior records reviewed: colonoscopy 2017 normal, Pap 2019 normal, mammogram 3/2020 normal. Next mammogram ordered for spring. Return 3 to 4 months.

documents.title: COVID-19 vaccine, dose 1 (pharmacy)
documents.author: pharmacy
documents.body: Retail pharmacy reports administration of Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine, dose 1 of 2, 3/27/2021, IM right deltoid. Imported from state registry.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, pt in her kitchen, consents to video care.
Check-in in place of an in-person visit this spring. Had COVID shot #1 on 3/27, sore arm only, #2 booked for 4/17. Feeling fine. Bought a home cuff after our last talk: readings she reads off are mostly 120s to low 130s over 70s to low 80s. Fasting sugars on the occasional check 130s to 150s.
No new symptoms.
A/P: T2DM, HTN by report controlled. Labs at the June visit in person. Mammogram scheduled? She will call radiology this week.

documents.title: COVID-19 vaccine, dose 2 (pharmacy)
documents.author: pharmacy
documents.body: Retail pharmacy reports administration of Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine, dose 2 of 2, 4/17/2021, IM right deltoid. Primary series complete. Imported from state registry.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here for diabetes/BP. Vaccinated now. Gardening most mornings. No complaints.
Never got to the spring mammogram; we'll fold it into the fall physical instead, old order cancelled.
Exam: BP as charted, heart and lungs normal, no edema.
Plan: same meds. A1c, BMP. Physical in September.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pt requesting 90-day refills on metformin, lisinopril, HCTZ and atorvastatin to the mail-order pharmacy her plan now prefers. Sent per protocol, PCP cosign. Pt aware.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
55F annual.
Interval: well. COVID primary series done in spring. No hospital or ED visits.
PMH: T2DM, HTN, postmenopausal. Meds unchanged x4. NKDA.
ROS: no chest pain, dyspnea, bowel change, bleeding, urinary complaints. Mood fine.
Exam: well appearing. HEENT partial edentulism. Thyroid normal. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Breasts deferred to mammography per pt preference. Abd benign. Skin no concerning lesions. Feet: monofilament intact, pulses good, no calluses.
PHQ-2 0.
A/P: preventive care. Mammogram ordered. Colonoscopy due 2027. Pap due 2022. Flu shot next month. CMP, lipids, A1c, UACR.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sheila, your physical labs look good. A1c steady, kidneys and liver normal, urine protein test normal, cholesterol where we want it. Nothing to change.

documents.title: Influenza vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine given IM left deltoid. No fever or illness today. Tolerated. Mammogram appointment confirmed for 11/3.

reports.text: Bilateral digital screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. Comparison March 2020. Breasts are scattered fibroglandular density. No suspicious mass, calcifications or architectural distortion. Skin and nipples normal.

documents.title: Mammogram result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Normal screening mammogram. Pt notified by portal. Repeat in a year.

documents.title: Diabetic eye exam report
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Annual dilated exam, DOS 12/1/2021. Best corrected acuity 20/25 each eye. Anterior segments quiet. Dilated fundus exam: no retinopathy, no macular edema, discs healthy. Return one year.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Long winter, admits more baking and less walking. Weight a bit up per scale. Meds taken. No symptoms.
Exam unremarkable, no edema, feet fine.
A1c drawn today; if it creeps up we talk about it, but metformin alone has been enough for years and she would rather work on food and walking first. Agreed.
F/u 3 months.

documents.title: A1c result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c a few tenths higher than fall. Discussed by portal: spring walking plan, recheck in June/July, no med change.

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt did not arrive for 10:00. Called, she had it on her calendar for next week. Apologized. Rebooked 7/11.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rescheduled from the missed visit. Back to walking 30 min most days since April. Home BPs fine. No hypoglycemia.
BP as charted. Exam unchanged.
A1c today. Continue metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, HCTZ 12.5, atorvastatin 20. Physical end of Sept with Pap.

reports.text: Liquid-based cervical cytology. Specimen adequate, transformation zone present. Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV not detected.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
56 yo F, preventive visit.
No interval illness. Walking regularly since spring, feels better for it.
Meds unchanged. NKDA.
ROS negative including GU and breast. No postmenopausal bleeding.
Exam: normal general exam. Pelvic: external genitalia normal for age, speculum exam with Pap/HPV collected, no lesions; bimanual without masses. Feet intact sensation, pulses 2+.
PHQ-2 0.
A/P: Pap/HPV today. Mammo ordered. Flu and updated COVID booster next month with RN. Labs. Colonoscopy 2027.

documents.title: Pap and lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Sheila, your Pap and HPV test are normal, so the next one isn't due for five years. Labs from the physical are also fine: A1c better than spring, blood counts, kidneys, liver and cholesterol normal. The walking is paying off.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine L deltoid, bivalent COVID booster R deltoid. Screening negative. Observed 15 min, fine.

reports.text: Bilateral screening mammogram with tomosynthesis, compared with 2021 and 2020. Scattered fibroglandular densities. No new mass, suspicious calcification or distortion.

documents.title: Mammogram
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Negative. Annual.

documents.title: Diabetic eye exam report
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Dilated retinal exam 11/30/2022 for diabetes. Acuity stable 20/25 OU. No hemorrhages, exudates or neovascularization; no retinopathy. Recheck 12 months.
